newsitem.title: USA: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS - up 1/4, trailing Treasuries.
newsitem.headline: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS - up 1/4, trailing Treasuries.

text.p: U.S. municipal bond prices were up about 1/4 point in quiet midday action, trailing Treasury market gains.

Traders said muni dealers are getting bogged down in trying to rid themselves of the week's new issues, and that investor resistance is keeping munis from fully sharing in the Treasury market rise. The long bond was up 16/32 at 98-28/32 to yield 6.59 percent.

In the muni secondary, bids on Metropolitan Pier and Exposition Authority, Ill., AMBAC 5-1/4s of 2027 were one basis point lower at 5.71 percent. Texas Turnpike Authority FGIC 5-1/4s of 2023 were down three basis points to 5.64 percent.

Debt futures were sharply higher. The March municipal contract jumped 26/32 to 115-18/32, while March T-bonds rose 19/32 to 113-3/32. The MOB spread widened to 79 ticks from 72 at the close on Thursday.

In new issue action, New York City said that it had received around $68 million of retail orders on Thursday, which was the first day of the presale period for an approximately $625 million bond sale to be priced on Tuesday.
Next week's new issue calendar includes $2.45 billion in 91 offerings, according to Reuters Municipal Bond Information Group.

Competitive sales total $731 million in 67 issues, with the largest issue a $130 million King County, Wash., issue on Monday. Negotiated sales total $1.7 billion in 24 offerings. The New York City deal, senior managed by Lehman Brothers, tops that list.
